cards.body:
Fort Pierce police identified Cornelius Trevon Ivory as the suspect accused of shooting and killing a 28-year-old man on South 14th Street the day after the Fourth of July, the department said Friday. Investigators obtained a warrant charging Ivory in connection with the shooting. Ivory was served with the warrant while in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail, where he is being held on unrelated charges.

The shooting occurred at about 3:43 a.m. on July 5. When officers arrived, they found two victims suffering from gunshot wounds. A woman had been shot in the hand, while the 28-year-old man suffered multiple gunshot wounds. He was taken to a hospital, where he later died.
cards.headline: Fort Pierce police identify suspect in deadly Fourth of July shooting
cards.teaser: The Fort Pierce Police Department identified the man accused of shooting and killing a 28-year-old man on South 14th Street the day after the Fourth of July.

cards.body:
Paige O'Donnell has legally surrendered the 36 Border Collies rescued from her Palm City home, the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast confirmed Friday. Staff will complete thorough medical testing and evaluations so adopters receive clear information about any long-term needs before placement decisions are made. The dogs also will be prepared for spay and neuter services, microchipping and vaccinations on a phased schedule alongside animals already in the shelter's care.

Adoption applications will be available on the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast's website and Facebook page beginning September 1. Applicants will be highly vetted to ensure appropriate matches, and applications for rescue groups also will be available beginning September 1. The shelter is asking the public not to call about the Border Collies at this time to keep phone lines available for urgent shelter needs and services.

O'Donnell faces 72 charges in what the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast calls the worst animal hoarding case it has ever seen. The dogs were rescued from her hoarded home in Palm City earlier this month. Deputies found the dogs living in deplorable conditions, with fur matted with feces and debris. Court documents show O'Donnell exhibited deceptive behavior during the investigation, blaming strong odors on missed trash collection and old seafood. Staff shaved 9 pounds off of one dog filled with feces and urine. Some dogs arrived with metal and glass fragments trapped in their fur.
cards.headline: Woman surrenders 36 Border Collies rescued from Palm City hoarding case
cards.teaser: Paige O'Donnell has legally surrendered the 36 Border Collies rescued from her Palm City home, clearing the way for the dogs to be adopted.

cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office arrested Matthew Waggle in connection with the fatal shooting of Dawn Kriskewic on First Street in Vero Beach early Sunday morning, Sheriff Eric Flowers announced at a news conference. Investigators believe Waggle traveled by bus to Orlando and then used an Uber to reach Vero Beach, where he allegedly shot Kriskewic and left the scene just 15 minutes later using the same method of transportation. He was there for 10, 15 minutes tops, Flowers said. He murdered her in cold blood in the street.

Flowers said Kriskewic had expressed concerns about Waggle to her co-workers at a hair salon. She had actually told her co-workers out at the hair salon, if he calls, if he shows up, I want nothing to do with him, tell him I'm not here, Flowers said. The sheriff credited the controversial Flock license plate reader system for helping locate Waggle. Without Flock, I'm not standing here four days later telling you about this guy being in custody in West Virginia, Flowers said. So for everybody who wants to talk about how bad this system is, we got a murderer behind bars because of this.

Waggle was found at a motel in West Virginia, and the gun used in the shooting belonged to Waggle's ex-wife. She was at the hotel, the same hotel that we got him at, Flowers said. So they were definitely in communication. We don't know to what extent, what she knew. We don't know if she knew his plans. All those are things that our detectives will be asking. The sheriff added that Waggle's ex-wife is still being questioned and is not currently facing any charges.
cards.headline: Indian River County Sheriff credits Flock camera system in Vero Beach murder arrest
cards.teaser: Sheriff Eric Flowers said the controversial license plate reader system helped authorities locate Matthew Waggle in West Virginia four days after the shooting death of Dawn Kriskewic.

hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released body camera footage showing U.S. Marshals arresting Matthew Waggle at a motel in West Virginia on Wednesday night. Waggle is accused of killing his ex-girlfriend, Dawn Kriskewic, in Vero Beach last Sunday. Kriskewic's body was discovered in front of her home on First Street, where she had been shot to death.

The video captures officers shouting commands during the arrest. Sheriff Eric Flowers said Waggle murdered Kriskewic in cold blood in the street. Kriskewic had told co-workers at her hair salon to turn Waggle away if he called or showed up, saying she wanted nothing to do with him.

At a news conference Thursday, Flowers explained that investigators believe Waggle traveled to Vero Beach from Orlando using an Uber, stayed just long enough to kill Kriskewic, and then left town in another Uber. Flowers credited the Flock license plate reader system for helping locate Waggle, saying without it he would not be announcing the arrest four days later.

Waggle remains in jail in West Virginia as authorities in Florida work on extraditing him back to Indian River County. The gun used in the shooting belonged to Waggle's ex-wife, who was at the same hotel where he was arrested. She is being questioned but is not currently facing charges.

The dogs were rescued from her hoarded home in Palm City earlier this month after a WPTV investigation helped renew the sheriff's office probe into the case. Deputies found the dogs living in deplorable conditions, with fur matted with feces and debris. Court documents show O'Donnell exhibited deceptive behavior during the investigation, blaming strong odors on missed trash collection and old seafood.

The dogs also will be prepared for spay/neuter services, microchipping and vaccinations on a phased schedule alongside animals already in the shelter's care. Adoption applications will be available at the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast's website and Facebook page beginning Sept. 1. During the initial rescue, shelter staff found lots of pieces of metal, rusted metal, sharp metal, and shards of glass stuck in the dogs' fur. cards.body:
Dezmone Karlde' Rome Johnson, 25, of Lauderhill was arrested July 31 by Broward County Sheriff's Office with help from the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force for the July 20 robbery at Royal Jewelers kiosk near the main entrance of Treasure Coast Square Mall in Jensen Beach. The Martin County Sheriff's Office says a crime scene unit lifted fingerprints and palm prints from the glass display counter and DNA from necklaces Johnson tried on and sunglasses that fell off while he ran. Those prints matched Johnson, who already had an open felony warrant for a probation violation at the time of the robbery. He recently bonded out of Broward County Jail on separate charges.

Deputies say Johnson asked to see several gold chains, tried some on, then left the mall before returning to ask for cheaper options. When the employee pulled out a new display holding nine gold chains, Johnson grabbed the entire display and ran through the same entrance, past a Ruby Tuesday and Port Barna Restaurant, and got into a silver Ford Fusion that headed south on Federal Highway. The stolen merchandise was worth more than $22,000. Three necklaces were recovered near the mall's south exit, leaving six chains valued at roughly $13,000 still missing.

Sheriff John Budensiek said Johnson has an extensive criminal history including prior arrests involving firearms charges and resisting. Budensiek warned that mall kiosks can be especially vulnerable since they typically have fewer security cameras and safeguards than storefront businesses, and said the mall has seen multiple snatch-and-grab incidents targeting kiosks this year. He encouraged vendors to ask for identification or proof of funds from customers requesting to see high-value merchandise.
cards.headline: Man accused of $22K gold chain grab at Treasure Coast Square Mall arrested, bonded out
cards.teaser: A Lauderhill man accused of snatching nine gold chains from a Jensen Beach mall kiosk was arrested through fingerprint and DNA evidence with help from U.S. Marshals. He bonded out shortly after his arrest on separate charges.

The Indian River County Sheriff's Office released body camera footage showing U.S. Marshals arresting Matthew Waggle at a motel in West Virginia on Wednesday night. The video captures officers shouting commands during the tense arrest. Waggle is accused of killing his ex-girlfriend, Dawn Kriskewic, in Vero Beach last Sunday. He remains in jail in West Virginia as authorities work on extraditing him back to Indian River County.

Kriskewic's body was discovered in front of her home on First Street. She had been shot to death. Investigators quickly identified Waggle as a person of interest. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said Kriskewic had told her co-workers at the hair salon that if Waggle called or showed up, she wanted nothing to do with him and asked them to tell him she was not there.

At a news conference Thursday, Flowers explained how investigators believe Waggle traveled to Vero Beach from Orlando using an Uber, stayed just long enough to kill Kriskewic, and then left town in another Uber. Flowers described the crime, saying Waggle murdered Kriskewic in cold blood in the street.

The body camera footage shows officers ordering Waggle to get down and give them his hands during the arrest at the West Virginia motel. Marshals placed Waggle in handcuffs during the operation. Authorities in Florida are now working on the extradition process to bring Waggle back to Indian River County to face charges.
